newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-NANTES CLIMB AMONG PACK CHASING MONACO.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NANTES CLIMB AMONG PACK CHASING MONACO.

text.p: Nantes beat 10-man Bastia 3-0 at home to extend their unbeaten run in the French first division to 21 matches on Saturday.
Bastia's Slovakian midfielder Lubomir Moravcik, recently back from a long layoff after breaking a leg, was sent off in the 23rd minute for retaliating to some tough tackling by the Nantes defence.
Japhet N'Doram took his league tally to 15 goals with the first in the 14th minute and Jocelyn Gourvennec, who now has 10, hit the second from a free kick two minutes before Moravcik's dismissal.

Tunisian international Adel Sellimi hit the third, his first goal since joining Nantes from Club Africain of Tunis at the start of the season, to send third-placed Bastia crashing to their worst defeat of the season.

Nantes' win greatly enhanced their hopes of a place in Europe next season as they joined a group of five teams separated by only four points and bunched behind leaders Monaco, who are six points clear.

Coach Jean-Claude Suaudeau, whose side won the championship in 1995, said: "Nantes were very strong collectively. There were passages (of play) that left me thinking we've rediscovered a very high standard of football."
Nantes had not won at home in their previous three matches at the Beaujoire stadium since mid-November, although they won their four away games during the same period.

"It's a very important victory because it puts us on course for Europe and because we resisted by remaining calm. It was a test of confidence," said teenage goalkeepeer Mickael Landreau, with a remarkable unbeaten record in his 19 consecutive first division games.

Bastia's coach Frederic Antonetti said: "We came on the field too nervous and the players argued too much with the referee. There was some unforgivable behaviour from Moravcik, who is an experienced player."
Monaco entertain defending champions Auxerre, while second-placed Paris St Germain are at home to Lyon on Sunday.

Bastia, one point behind PSG, are also just one point ahead of Bordeaux, who drew 1-1 at fifth-placed Strasbourg in a dress rehearsal of next month's League Cup final. But the Corsicans have a game in hand.

Veteran Jean-Pierre Papin put Bordeaux ahead with a 19th minute penalty, his ninth goal of the season, but the division's top scorer David Zitelli, now on 18, equalised 10 minutes later after Pascal Nouma opened up the defence on the right.
Marseille slipped further away from a first place in Europe since their 1993 European Cup triumph when they fell 3-1 at Guingamp. They have yet to win away this season.

Guingamp's Romanian left back Gheorghe Mihali scored twice in the first half, both from free kicks by playmaker Stephane Carnot. Carnot scored the third in the 58th minute, four minutes after striker Marc Libbra pulled one back for Marseille.
Caen's Frederic Nee hit the fastest goal of the season in the 14th second of their home relegation clash with Lille which they won 1-0.

Former Ireland international Tony Cascarino kept Nancy level with Caen with the only goal in their 1-0 home win over bottom club Nice, who are now six points adrift. But Nancy are still one from bottom behind Caen on goal difference.
